# Instructor guide · Topic 14: Binary Search Trees

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Use the BST property to search, insert and delete in O(h), validate a BST correctly, and know why balance matters.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **The BST property:** For every node, everything in its left subtree is smaller and everything in its right subtree is larger.
- **Search and insert:** Compare with the current node, go left or right, repeat.
- **Delete:** Leaf: remove it.
- **Balance and shape:** All BST operations cost O(h).
- **Using sorted order:** Inorder = sorted.
- **Build a BST from scratch:** Insert, search, inorder, min, max, delete and height in one class.

## Duration and prerequisites

- Lessons: about **60 minutes** of guided material (6 lessons)
- Practice: 14 coding problems and 25 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 13 (Trees), Topic 11 (Searching)

Open the topic in the browser (`#t/bst`) and project it; every lesson alternates a short explanation with questions the class answers together.

## Live coding demonstrations

- Code the first “Code it” problem of each lesson live, thinking aloud.
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Kth Smallest: sort everything → stop early in inorder** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: Binary search tree: insert, search, delete

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- BST property?
- Search cost?
- Delete with two children?
- Validate correctly?
- Sorted order?
- Why balanced trees?

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Search in a BST (`bst-search`)
- Insert into a BST (`bst-insert`)
- Minimum and Maximum (`bst-min-max`)

Code tracing on the board: Insert, then inorder (`bst-p1`), Inserting sorted data (`bst-p2`), The search path (`bst-p3`), Smallest value (`bst-p4`)

Find-the-bug warm-ups: Only checking the children (`bst-d1`), The new node vanishes (`bst-d2`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- Validate a BST (`bst-validate`)
- Kth Smallest in a BST (`bst-kth`)
- Build from scratch: Build a Binary Search Tree (`build-bst`)

## Homework

- Lowest Common Ancestor in a BST (`bst-lca`)
- Sorted List to Balanced BST (`bst-sorted-to-bst`)
- Recover a BST (`bst-recover`)
- Finish the topic's Review quiz in the browser and clear the revision queue.

## Solutions and grading

- Reference solutions: `solutions/14_bst/` (also behind “Show solution” in the browser).
- Students check their own work with `python dsa.py test <id>`; collect `pytest tests/test_my_solutions.py -k bst` output as evidence.
- Grade with the coding rubric in [README.md](README.md#grading-rubrics).
